title_en: 7 Red Dead Redemption Easter Eggs in GTA 6 -The Definitive Proof That Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption Share The Same Universe
summary_en: Here are the seven easter eggs in GTA 6 that prove Red Dead Redemption and Grand Theft Auto take place in the same universe.
body_en:
From action movies to popular memes, there are dozens and dozens of Easter eggs and references to wider pop culture in GTA 6. But Rockstar has also slipped in more than a few nods to some of the studio’s previous games within Leonida. There’s a Manhunt-themed tattoo, for example, and a ludicrously convoluted secret that has already been unearthed involving a portal back to the days of Vice City. But one series is showing up more than others: Red Dead Redemption.
We’re still working our way through finding all of them, as is the rest of the internet, but so far we’ve found seven secrets that relate to the developer’s beloved Western games. From hats and guns to road names and license plates, here are seven Red Dead Easter eggs in GTA 6.
If you’re looking for hidden details about Red Dead, the Western-themed Frontier Mini Golf course is a natural place to start. While none of the holes directly tell the tale of Red Dead Revolver, Red Dead Redemption, or its prequel—aside from squinting at hole four and seeing a snowy train wreck as a tangential nod to RDR2’s prologue—there are still things to find.
We’ll get on to who can be seen roaming it in a moment, but before you even set foot inside, an Easter egg can be found. That’s because the attraction itself is located on Valentine Drive, a reference to the first major town you explore in Chapter 1 of Red Dead Redemption 2’s story. This is the location where Arthur famously drinks a few too many beers, has a bit of a dance, and looks for his friend, Lenny. Sadly, alcohol doesn’t seem to be served at this Mini Golf, although there’s nothing stopping you from bringing your own six-pack in.
Once you’re on the course, though, a little friend with a familiar face riding on his back may well walk up to you. A small chihuahua with a cowboy toy, dressed in remarkably similar clothing to what Red Dead Redemption 2 protagonist Arthur Morgan wore in many of the game’s trailers. Feel free to give the little guy a pet, too, and his gun-toting rider will look like he’s giving it a little “yeehaw”. Adorable.
Perhaps more life-sized Arthur Morgan Easter eggs are more your thing, though. Well, get yourself over to Port Gellhorn to get your hands on, and head in, one such thing. Follow the trail of signs and balloons to find a resident looking to get rid of any old tat. Hidden amongst it all, though, is a real treasure. No, not the cow-patterned Hawaiian shirt, but something that will make fans of Red Dead Redemption 2’s hearts flutter a little: a genuine cowboy hat. Not just any cowboy, either, but Arthur himself. The dark brown colour, complete with twisted rope around the rim, is unmistakable, and is now Jason or Lucia’s to wear whenever they like. An absolute bargain at $35, too.
As if we needed any further proof that the Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption stories take place in the same universe, the Duke Arms Company cements this. At any of Leonida’s Ammu-Nation stores, you can find weapons made by the same gun company that produced the Duke 1853 Navy Revolver in Red Dead Online. On the packaging found inside GTA 6’s gun stores, you can also spot 1853 written out in Roman numerals (MDCCCLIII) on the boxes. It just can’t be a coincidence.
“The Cowboy’s Prayer is To Die Young” is a Wild West-set novel of which you can read a few pages in GTA 6. There are a few fun little details hidden within. First, a mention of Blackwater, the port city from Red Dead Redemption and its prequel, where John Marston chooses to build his ranch near to. But there’s also a familiar name to those who chose to fully engage with RDR2’s side activities.
Flaco Hernández was an infamous outlaw who you can meet during the 2018 game’s “The Noblest of Men, and a Woman” stranger mission. At the end of that story, you knock on his cabin by Cairn Lake and defeat him in a duel. The book in GTA 6 recounts all of these details, confirming that the events of Rockstar’s Western games are canon in Grand Theft Auto lore. There are many copies of the book to be found around Leonida, but I spotted one at the Grayson Motel towards the north of the map in Lummox County.
More locations from Red Dead here, as you may have spotted some vehicles roaming around Leonida that don’t sport license plates belonging to the “Goodtime State”. In fact, some of them hail from New Austin, the sandy state in Red Dead Redemption where the likes of Armadillo, Tumbleweed, and Thieves’ Landing can be found. Unfortunately, you can’t add one of these to your own car at a GTA 6 mod shop, but you can always jack someone else’s ride if you want to pretend you’re from the cowboy-adjacent state.
And finally, more of a fun wink to the camera than a full-on Easter egg, there’s a band playing live shows in Leonida that must be a fan of Rockstar’s western games. Get yourself over to the Three Sheets liquor store in the starting area of Key Lento to take a look at a poster for the Rad Dads’ show. They’re heading out on a redemption tour. Rad Dads Redemption. Red Dead Redemption. Get it? There’s not much more to say about this one than that, really.
And those are the Red Dead secrets that we’ve found so far in GTA 6. Did we miss any? Let us know in the comments.
